title: Developer in an organization buying an API
instance: Oct 13: the split the room agreed to. Nicole [00:40:13] “We can definitely split that out.” The seller wants the org, not the person: Melodie [00:30:58].

A.label: org delegates to the developer
A.sub: the developer is a local identifier inside the org (Melodie 00:32:18) · limits a separate note

A2.label: the developer sets the agent's scope

B.label: this seller's profile: the org ID, verifiable
B.sub: the 402 states the payment terms and the org affiliation it needs (Melodie 00:31:20) · the answer: the signed payload plus a verifiable org identifier · the developer's own identity is not asked for

C.label: the wallet address is the identifier anchor
C.sub: authorization.from · which account, not which org

C2.label: the identifier is linked to the org's entity ID (4.2.1)
C2.sub: a domain or LEI the seller can verify · the developer's local id: org-held or passed to the seller (T5)

E.label: trace a transaction to a user in the org
E.sub: even though the user's verified identity never left the org (Nicole 00:36:47)

differs: Differs from K0 in the Principal lane (an organization) and in A, B, C (org affiliation, not the person).
slots: Org delegates to the developer, who scopes the agent

Alfred [00:37:32] “they might already have a data model where they have an org, and they have a specific user with team members, and then the agent.” The developer is a local identifier the org keeps (Melodie [00:32:18] “We have local UUIDs or things like that.”).
This seller’s profile: which org, and is it approved

Melodie [00:31:20] “we care about having some kind of affiliation between the requester and the entity, just to… for us to know that the entity in itself has been approved.” Fields dial: org ID. Assurance dial: verifiable.
The wallet is the anchor; the org is the identity it links to
The link from wallet to org entity ID is RFP 4.2.1. Whether the developer’s local identifier also travels to the seller is tension T5; both readings are drawn in Phase 4.
Trace back to a user in the org
Nicole [00:36:47] “I also want to be able to trace back certain transactions to a particular user in my organization”. Held on the org side.
footer: The payload names a wallet. Nothing says which organization controls it, or that the developer running the agent may spend its funds.
Org affiliation in B, the wallet in C with the link to the org’s entity ID; the person stays inside the org.
Provable: Melodie [00:38:04] “the good thing about an org is that you can have, like, easy means of having publicly verifiable data.”
Who holds the developer-to-org mapping (T5) · whether this case is really the B2B flow (Adrian, chat 00:33:13, unanswered) · whether delegated authority is in scope (TSC).
